name: SkillEvaluator
description: Multi-tier framework for evaluating AI agent skills and plugins with quality gates, security scanning, harness compatibility checks, semantic overlap detection, synthetic evaluation dataset generation, and live agent evaluation that measures how skills affect agent behavior. Ships reusable CI templates that bring every check to any repository.
readmeExcerpt:
#

Evaluate and improve AI agent skills and plugins: quality, security, overlap, compatibility, and real impact across agents

> 📺 **Livestream:** [Ask the Experts: Evaluating Agent Skills](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4rI0zATFxYI) SkillEvaluator checks AI agent skills and plugins, and measures a skill's effect on task results: start with quality checks, then compare runs with and without a skill. Catch skill issues before merge. Connect your repository to SkillEvaluator with a [CI template](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/repository-integration) for automated quality and security gates, without building or maintaining evaluation code. Agent skills are folders of instructions and supporting files defined by the [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/). SkillEvaluator is part of the [NVIDIA Verified Skills pipeline](https://github.com/NVIDIA/skills). ## Get started Install the CLI in a Python 3.12–3.14 environment: ```bash pip install skillevaluator ```
Or use uv ```bash uv tool install --python 3.13 skillevaluator ```
For uv setup or direct GitHub source installation, see [Installation](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/installation). Then check skills from your terminal, CI, or agent:

Run checks backed by **500+ static rules and detection patterns**, without an LLM key. Complete [scanner setup](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/installation-options#system-tools) for full coverage: ```bash skillevaluator validate \ ./my-skill --tiers 1 ```
Run all three tiers After [all-tier setup with NVIDIA Build](#run-all-three-tiers-with-a-free-nvidia-build-key), remove `--tiers 1` to add deduplication and live agent evaluation to measure skill lift: ```bash skillevaluator validate \ ./my-skill ```

Check every skill change. Run in your GitHub repo to open a setup PR: ```bash skillevaluator ci init ``` **Start here:** [Guided setup for GitHub and GitLab](#bring-skill-evaluation-to-your-repository).

Add the skill to Claude Code, Codex or another agent: ```bash npx skills add \ NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator ``` Then ask: *"Is my skill any good?"* See the [agent guide](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/agent-skill).
### ⚡ [Harness check](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/harness-check): will your agent load your skill? 🔑 **No API key** · 🤖 **No agent run** ```bash skillevaluator harness-check ./my-skill ``` Illustrative summary of versioned profiles. Full output can include notes and schema diagnostics. ```text ╭─ Harness compatibility · my-skill ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ │ ⚠️ codex degraded Description cut to 1,021 chars + '...' in the skill list │ │ ❌ claude-code not loaded .agents/skills is not scanned │ │ ✅ opencode loads │ │ ✅ hermes loads │ │ ✅ openclaw loads │ │ ❌ copilot-cli not loaded description is 1,028 UTF-16 units, 4 over the 1,024 limit │ ╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ❌ 2 of 6 not loaded ─╯ ``` `skillevaluator validate` includes Harness Check in Tier 1 alongside **quality, schema, version, PII, license, Unicode and script linting**. Security and code integrity checks use **SkillSpector, Gitleaks, Bandit and optional Semgrep**. [See all Tier 1 checks](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/tier1-reference#the-checks); use `--tiers 1` to run only this tier. 🧪 **Ready to go deeper?** Try a [live agent evaluation](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/tier3-live-evaluation) (Tier 3). ## Quickstart ### Check your skill without a key ```bash skillevaluator quality-check ./my-skill ``` No API key, scanner, GPU or Docker is needed. It prints a score out of 100 with a grade and the findings behind it; the passing threshold defaults to 70. This is static quality only; publication evidence stays `INCOMPLETE`. Security and agent impact need additional checks. See the [keyless walkthrough](docs/quickstart.mdx#run-without-an-llm). No skill yet? Clone the repository and use the bundled `src/skillevaluator/tier3/reference_skills/text-analyzer`. Scores can differ by release. ### Run all three tiers with a free NVIDIA Build key Eligible NVIDIA Developer Program members can use NVIDIA-hosted endpoints for **free prototyping**, subject to [access terms and rate limits](https://docs.api.nvidia.com/nim/docs/product). 1. Sign in at [build.nvidia.com](https://build.nvidia.com/) and complete enrollment. 2. Open a model page, select **Get API Key**, and generate your key. 3. Complete [scanner setup](docs/installation-options.mdx#system-tools), start Docker, and [prepare a reviewed dataset](docs/prepare-dataset.mdx). Install every tier, set the provider and key, then validate: ```bash python -m pip install "skillevaluator[all]" export SKILL_EVAL_LLM_PROVIDER=nv_build export NVIDIA_API_KEY='nvapi-...' skillevaluator validate ./my-skill ``` Without `--tiers`, `validate` runs all three. The key covers embeddings and chat in Tier 2 and supported agents in Tier 3; add `--llm` for model checks in Tier 1. For uv or GitHub installations, use the matching [all-tier install](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/installation#all-tiers) instead of the pip command above. Tier 3 also needs Docker running; add `--tiers 1,2` to skip it. More in [Run the combined pipeline](#run-the-combined-pipeline), the [Build walkthrough](docs/quickstart.mdx#use-nvidia-build) and [provider configuration](docs/configuration.mdx). ## Bring skill evaluation to your repository > **Start here: [Repository integration guide](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/repository-integration)**, > install to first passing check on GitHub or GitLab. Below is the summary. **Minimal setup. No evaluation code to write or maintain.** Choose your skill folders and thresholds to get automated validation, security scanning and downloadable reports for changed skills in GitHub or GitLab. **[11 CI checks](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/tier1-reference#the-checks) backed by 500+ static rules and detection patterns:** quality, schema, version, PII, license, Unicode, script linting, [Harness Check](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/harness-check), security, code integrity and dependency auditing.
**Scanners:** [SkillSpector](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/tier1-reference#security--vulnerability-scanning), [Gitleaks, Bandit and Semgrep](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/tier1-reference#code-integrity--code-risk-secrets-and-hygiene), and [pip-audit](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/tier1-reference#dependency--cve-audit-opt-in). **GitHub guided setup:** after [installing the CLI](#get-started), run inside your checked-out repository: ```bash skillevaluator ci init ``` Choose checks and optional hosted feedback, then review the setup PR. [CLI setup guide](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/cli-onboarding). **Manual setup (no CLI):** copy a filled-in template from [CI templates](ci/bundles/README.md). | Your repository | Ready-to-use template | Copy destination | | --- | --- | --- | | GitHub | [Skill checks](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/blob/main/ci/bundles/1.2.1/skill-checks.yml) | `.github/workflows/skill-checks.yml` | | GitLab | [Skill checks](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/blob/main/ci/bundles/1.2.1/gitlab-skill-checks.yml) | `.gitlab-ci.yml`, or merge into your existing pipeline | | GitHub PR comments without hosting | [Optional comments](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/blob/main/ci/bundles/1.2.1/comment-skill-checks.yml) | Second workflow; complete [comment setup](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/blob/main/ci/bundles/1.2.1/README.md#pr-comment-setup) | | GitHub hosted reports and PR comments | [Optional publisher](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/blob/main/ci/bundles/1.2.1/publish-skill-reports.yml) | Second workflow; complete [publisher setup](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/blob/main/ci/bundles/1.2.1/README.md#one-time-publisher-setup) | Pick one optional feedback workflow. These run Tier 1 checks without a model key; [all-tier CI setup](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/advanced-ci) adds deduplication and live agent evaluation. Also: [template reference](ci/templates/README.md) and [report examples](ci/examples/README.md). ## Three-tier overview Each tier is independent. Use the [all-tier installation](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/installation#all-tiers) for all three: | Tier | Question | Example after setup | Additional setup | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Tier 1: Validation | Is the skill safe, well-formed and [harness-compatible](docs/tier1-reference.mdx#the-checks)? | `skillevaluator tier1 ./my-skill --no-llm` | External scanners for full static coverage; a provider and model clients enable LLM checks | | Tier 1: Harness Check | Will the agent load the skill? | `skillevaluator harness-check ./my-skill` | No API key or agent run | | Tier 2: Deduplication | Does guidance repeat or overlap? | `skillevaluator tier2 ./my-skill` | Embeddings and chat; add `--catalog ./skill-catalog.json` for inter-skill comparison | | Tier 3: Live Agent Evaluation | Does the skill help the agent? | `skillevaluator tier3 ./my-skill` | Provider access, a supported agent, and a running sandbox (Docker by default) | Prepare [scanners](docs/installation-options.mdx#system-tools) for your installed release; Semgrep is optional. `--no-llm` does not remove scanner requirements; a scanner that cannot run is `INCOMPLETE` and exits nonzero. [SkillSpector](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillSpector) provides specialized skill security scanning; [Harbor](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor), the open-source agent evaluation framework, powers sandboxed agent runs. Tier 2 reports when inter-skill comparison did not run. Tier 3 autopilot reuses sources or creates one skill-grounded case with limited coverage. See [tier guides](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/). ## Run the combined pipeline After setting up the provider, scanners, and agent sandbox, run all three tiers: ```bash skillevaluator doctor --env-mode docker skillevaluator validate ./my-skill ``` `doctor` checks readiness, not inference success. `validate` runs all tiers with autopilot for skills. Use `--tiers 1,2` to skip live evaluation or `--tiers 1` for static checks. `--no-autopilot` requires an existing source. Other artifact types retain their applicable stages. Tier 1 gates `validate`. Tier 2 gates unless `--no-block-on-dedup` is set; Tier 3 gates only with `--block-on-agent-eval`. releases.name: SkillEvaluator v0.9.0
releases.body:
# SkillEvaluator 0.9.0

SkillEvaluator 0.9.0 expands how you build evaluation datasets, compare skill versions, and understand why an agent passed or failed. It adds controls for evaluation budgets, reusable baselines, and clearer evidence across terminal, HTML, JSON, Markdown, and benchmark reports.

For PyPI users upgrading from 0.7.2, this release also includes the changes shipped in the GitHub-only 0.8.0 release.

## Highlights

- **Build and review better evaluation datasets.** Declare deterministic checks for script execution, workspace files, and final responses. Generate datasets grounded in skill instructions, author intent, or traces; import production traces as redacted review candidates; and promote expectations only after explicit human review. Preview legacy dataset migrations before writing a new file.
- **Track skill improvements over time.** Compare retained skill versions with `--compare-to` and `compare-versions`, browse run history, and reuse a compatible no-skill baseline with `--reuse-baseline`. Version comparisons remain separate from Skill Lift against a no-skill baseline.
- **Control evaluation spending.** Set token, judge-call, attempt, and priced-cost bud

releases.name: SkillEvaluator v0.8.0
releases.body:
# SkillEvaluator 0.8.0

Tier 3 now computes every score from judge verdicts, grades accuracy on the outcome alone, and explains failing scores in the HTML report. A new `tier3 feedback` chat answers questions about a completed run, and opt-in policies control which models a judge may fall back to. Reports give every finding stable IDs. Tier 1 accepts audited SkillSpector baselines and evidence-bound PII waivers. This release also ships a rebuilt Tier 1 scanner image and CI bundle.

```bash
pip install --upgrade skillevaluator
skillevaluator ci init
```

[PyPI package](https://pypi.org/project/skillevaluator/0.8.0/) · [CLI onboarding guide](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/cli-onboarding) · [Ready-to-use CI templates](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/tree/v0.8.0/ci/bundles/0.8.0)

## Before you upgrade

- **The shared validation policy is now `default`** ([#334](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/pull/334)). The shared OSS policy for public and private repositories was called `external`. `--profile external`, `--external`, and `SKILLEVALUATOR_PROFILE=external` still work, with the same rules. Report policy metadata and the policy digest change

readmeHtml:
Evaluate and improve AI agent skills and plugins: quality, security, overlap, compatibility, and real impact across agents

📺 Livestream: Ask the Experts: Evaluating Agent Skills

SkillEvaluator checks AI agent skills and plugins, and measures a skill's effect on task results: start with quality checks, then compare runs with and without a skill.

Catch skill issues before merge. Connect your repository to SkillEvaluator with a CI template for automated quality and security gates, without building or maintaining evaluation code.

Agent skills are folders of instructions and supporting files defined by the Agent Skills specification. SkillEvaluator is part of the NVIDIA Verified Skills pipeline.

Get started

Install the CLI in a Python 3.12–3.14 environment:

pip install skillevaluator
Or use uv 
uv tool install --python 3.13 skillevaluator

For uv setup or direct GitHub source installation, see Installation.

Then check skills from your terminal, CI, or agent:

Run checks backed by 500+ static rules and detection patterns, without an LLM key. Complete scanner setup for full coverage:

skillevaluator validate \
  ./my-skill --tiers 1
Run all three tiers

After all-tier setup with NVIDIA Build, remove --tiers 1 to add deduplication and live agent evaluation to measure skill lift:

skillevaluator validate \
  ./my-skill

Check every skill change. Run in your GitHub repo to open a setup PR:

skillevaluator ci init

Start here: Guided setup for GitHub and GitLab.

Add the skill to Claude Code, Codex or another agent:

npx skills add \
  NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator

Then ask: "Is my skill any good?" See the agent guide.

⚡ Harness check: will your agent load your skill?

🔑 No API key · 🤖 No agent run

skillevaluator harness-check ./my-skill

Illustrative summary of versioned profiles. Full output can include notes and schema diagnostics.

╭─ Harness compatibility · my-skill ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│  ⚠️ codex        degraded    Description cut to 1,021 chars + '...' in the skill list   │
│  ❌ claude-code  not loaded  .agents/skills is not scanned                              │
│  ✅ opencode     loads                                                                  │
│  ✅ hermes       loads                                                                  │
│  ✅ openclaw     loads                                                                  │
│  ❌ copilot-cli  not loaded  description is 1,028 UTF-16 units, 4 over the 1,024 limit  │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ❌ 2 of 6 not loaded ─╯

skillevaluator validate includes Harness Check in Tier 1 alongside quality, schema, version, PII, license, Unicode and script linting. Security and code integrity checks use SkillSpector, Gitleaks, Bandit and optional Semgrep. See all Tier 1 checks; use --tiers 1 to run only this tier.

🧪 Ready to go deeper? Try a live agent evaluation (Tier 3).

Quickstart

Check your skill without a key

skillevaluator quality-check ./my-skill

No API key, scanner, GPU or Docker is needed. It prints a score out of 100 with a grade and the findings behind it; the passing threshold defaults to 70. This is static quality only; publication evidence stays INCOMPLETE. Security and agent impact need additional checks. See the keyless walkthrough.

No skill yet? Clone the repository and use the bundled src/skillevaluator/tier3/reference_skills/text-analyzer. Scores can differ by release.

Run all three tiers with a free NVIDIA Build key

Eligible NVIDIA Developer Program members can use NVIDIA-hosted endpoints for free prototyping, subject to access terms and rate limits.

  1. Sign in at build.nvidia.com and complete enrollment.
  2. Open a model page, select Get API Key, and generate your key.
  3. Complete scanner setup, start Docker, and prepare a reviewed dataset. Install every tier, set the provider and key, then validate:
python -m pip install "skillevaluator[all]"
export SKILL_EVAL_LLM_PROVIDER=nv_build
export NVIDIA_API_KEY='nvapi-...'
skillevaluator validate ./my-skill

Without --tiers, validate runs all three. The key covers embeddings and chat in Tier 2 and supported agents in Tier 3; add --llm for model checks in Tier 1. For uv or GitHub installations, use the matching all-tier install instead of the pip command above. Tier 3 also needs Docker running; add --tiers 1,2 to skip it. More in Run the combined pipeline, the Build walkthrough and provider configuration.

Bring skill evaluation to your repository

Start here: Repository integration guide, install to first passing check on GitHub or GitLab. Below is the summary.

Minimal setup. No evaluation code to write or maintain. Choose your skill folders and thresholds to get automated validation, security scanning and downloadable reports for changed skills in GitHub or GitLab.

11 CI checks backed by 500+ static rules and detection patterns: quality, schema, version, PII, license, Unicode, script linting, Harness Check, security, code integrity and dependency auditing.
Scanners: SkillSpector, Gitleaks, Bandit and Semgrep, and pip-audit.

GitHub guided setup: after installing the CLI, run inside your checked-out repository:

skillevaluator ci init

Choose checks and optional hosted feedback, then review the setup PR. CLI setup guide.

Manual setup (no CLI): copy a filled-in template from CI templates.

Your repository Ready-to-use template Copy destination
GitHub Skill checks .github/workflows/skill-checks.yml
GitLab Skill checks .gitlab-ci.yml, or merge into your existing pipeline
GitHub PR comments without hosting Optional comments Second workflow; complete comment setup
GitHub hosted reports and PR comments Optional publisher Second workflow; complete publisher setup

Pick one optional feedback workflow. These run Tier 1 checks without a model key; all-tier CI setup adds deduplication and live agent evaluation.

Also: template reference and report examples.

Three-tier overview

Each tier is independent. Use the all-tier installation for all three:

Tier Question Example after setup Additional setup
Tier 1: Validation Is the skill safe, well-formed and harness-compatible? skillevaluator tier1 ./my-skill --no-llm External scanners for full static coverage; a provider and model clients enable LLM checks
Tier 1: Harness Check Will the agent load the skill? skillevaluator harness-check ./my-skill No API key or agent run
Tier 2: Deduplication Does guidance repeat or overlap? skillevaluator tier2 ./my-skill Embeddings and chat; add --catalog ./skill-catalog.json for inter-skill comparison
Tier 3: Live Agent Evaluation Does the skill help the agent? skillevaluator tier3 ./my-skill Provider access, a supported agent, and a running sandbox (Docker by default)

Prepare scanners for your installed release; Semgrep is optional. --no-llm does not remove scanner requirements; a scanner that cannot run is INCOMPLETE and exits nonzero. SkillSpector provides specialized skill security scanning; Harbor, the open-source agent evaluation framework, powers sandboxed agent runs.

Tier 2 reports when inter-skill comparison did not run. Tier 3 autopilot reuses sources or creates one skill-grounded case with limited coverage. See tier guides.

Run the combined pipeline

After setting up the provider, scanners, and agent sandbox, run all three tiers:

skillevaluator doctor --env-mode docker
skillevaluator validate ./my-skill

doctor checks readiness, not inference success. validate runs all tiers with autopilot for skills. Use --tiers 1,2 to skip live evaluation or --tiers 1 for static checks. --no-autopilot requires an existing source. Other artifact types retain their applicable stages.

Tier 1 gates validate. Tier 2 gates unless --no-block-on-dedup is set; Tier 3 gates only with --block-on-agent-eval. Model and managed-sandbox usage can incur charges; see runtime and cost.

Standalone generation needs substantive evals/EVAL.md guidance, a --prompt file with task requests and outcomes, or matching retained traces. --force below replaces the autopilot starter; --refine refines it. Explicit --grounding skill permits skill-only starters. Review cases; templates omit unauthored negatives.

skillevaluator tier3 create-eval-dataset ./my-skill --full --prompt eval-guidance.md --force

Run from a source checkout

For an editable environment, follow the development setup.

Research and citation

Resources: paper, PDF, DOI, BibTeX, and NVIDIA Developer blog. Cite the paper and record the SkillEvaluator release or commit; see CITATION.cff.

Documentation

See the documentation for setup, tier guides, reports, CI integration, CLI reference, and performance dashboard.

Installation and third-party software

This project will download and install additional third-party open source software projects. Review the license terms of these open source projects before use.

Contributing

Read CONTRIBUTING.md and run:

make lint && make test && make build

See project governance and Code of Conduct.

Support

Support level: Experimental. Community-supported, best-effort, with no SLA or NVIDIA enterprise support entitlement. Report bugs and feature requests through GitHub Issues; see SUPPORT.md.

Security

Report suspected vulnerabilities using the private process in SECURITY.md. Do not disclose security issues in a public GitHub issue.

Releases

See CHANGELOG.md and GitHub Releases.

License

Apache License 2.0: see LICENSE, NOTICE, and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

aiSummary.oneLiner: Multi‑tier framework that validates AI agent skills and quantifies their effect on task performance
aiSummary.whatItDoes: SkillEvaluator addresses the lack of systematic quality and impact assessment for AI agent skills defined by the Agent Skills specification. It implements a three‑tier pipeline—static validation, semantic deduplication, and live agent evaluation—each optional and runnable via a single CLI. Tier 1 runs safety and format checks using SkillSpector, Gitleaks, and optional Semgrep without requiring an LLM. Tier 2 computes embedding‑based overlap to detect redundant guidance across a catalog of skills. Tier 3 executes the skill in a sandboxed agent (Harbor) and measures performance changes, optionally using NVIDIA Build LLMs for rubric scoring. The framework produces deterministic JSON or CLI reports and can be integrated in CI or invoked programmatically.
keyFeatures: Tier‑1 validation: Performs safety, format, and harness compatibility checks with SkillSpector and Gitleaks without an LLM.
Tier‑2 deduplication: Uses embedding models to detect semantic overlap between a skill and a catalog, flagging redundant guidance.
Tier‑3 live evaluation: Runs the skill in a sandboxed agent environment and reports impact on task success metrics.
CLI integration: Single command interface supports pip, uv, and CI workflows, producing JSON and human‑readable outputs.
Provider flexibility: Works keyless or with NVIDIA Build, allowing LLM‑backed rubric scoring via environment variables.

useCases.title: CI quality gate for skill repositories
useCases.description: Teams can add `skillevaluator ci init` to their GitHub pipelines to automatically reject skills that fail static safety or format checks before merge.

useCases.title: Skill marketplace curation
useCases.description: Marketplace operators run the full three‑tier pipeline to ensure submitted skills are non‑redundant and demonstrably improve agent performance, providing a quantitative grade.

useCases.title: Research benchmarking of agent capabilities
useCases.description: Researchers generate synthetic evaluation datasets with `tier3 create-eval-dataset` and compare how different skill sets affect benchmark tasks.

useCases.title: Secure plugin development
useCases.description: Developers of agent plugins use Tier 1 scans to catch insecure code patterns and missing license headers early in the development cycle.

useCases.title: Custom agent integration
useCases.description: Deployers add the skill to Claude Code or Codex via `npx skills add` and let the agent query SkillEvaluator to decide whether to use the skill at runtime.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: SkillEvaluator is aimed at AI agent developers, skill marketplace curators, and CI engineers who need automated quality and impact testing of Agent Skills. Users should be comfortable with Python, command‑line tools, and optionally have access to NVIDIA Build API keys for LLM‑backed rubrics.
